tagline: Downriver from New Orleans to the fishing boats at Shell Beach.
intro: Highway 46 leaves New Orleans on St. Claude Avenue, crosses into St. Bernard Parish and runs downriver through Arabi and Chalmette. Then it turns east past the turnings for Yscloskey and Hopedale, comes to Shell Beach and stops at a dead end on the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet Canal.

The byway takes its name from San Bernardo, one of four settlements founded by Canary Islanders who came to Spanish Louisiana between 1778 and 1783. Of the four it kept the most of its old ways, and the Canarian Spanish of the 1700s is still spoken in the parish. In the town of St. Bernard six museum houses keep the Isleño story.

moments.title: Arabi
moments.text: The town began as Stockyard Landing, and people digging swimming pools in Old Arabi have turned up dishes from New Orleans hotels whose table scraps once fed the animals.

moments.title: Chalmette Battlefield
moments.text: Beside the field where Andrew Jackson's troops beat the British in 1815 stood Fazendeville, an African American village of shotgun houses, razed in the 1960s to make the battlefield park larger.

moments.title: Shell Beach
moments.text: Near the end of the highway, on the Gulf Outlet canal by Lake Borgne, shrimp and oyster fishermen can be seen hoisting their nets.
